docs.purpose: Shows an admin the log of push notifications sent to users, newest first and paginated, and — when a specific user is selected — that user's registered devices, notification preferences, and the current on/off switches for the notification system.
docs.data_story: It reads 5 tables — `notification_dispatches`, `notifications`, `device_tokens`, `user_profiles` and `logic_variables` and writes nothing. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 2 places: `admin_user_detail`, `admin_notifications`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `QUERY`. It declares its `database.reads[]` with named columns, its response projection as an explicit whitelist, its auth class, its rate bucket and its staleness — and `outputs.writes` is forced to `"none"`. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: Dispatch rows return as `{...r, push_token: maskPushToken(r.push_token)}` — a raw-row spread with one field redacted, not a whitelist. Push tokens are always masked to the last 6 characters before leaving the server. The 'gates' block is a READ-ONLY surface of three logic_variables kill-switch/throttle keys; the write path is the Control Panel tool, not this route. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: Census checklist: all 5 named tables VERIFIED. Census MISSED `profiles` (verifyAdminAuth, src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:117-120). FINDINGS: (1) The WHERE fragment is assembled by string concatenation at :63 and interpolated into the SQL at :80, but the value is bound as $3 (:64) — parameterised, not injectable; the fragment itself is a fixed literal. (2) TYPE SAFETY — the per-user block is typed `let user: unknown` at :97 and the prefs query at :104 is untyped (`pool.query` with no row generic), so prefs reaches the client unvalidated; there is no response-side Zod parse anywhere in this route, unlike the watchlist routes (contrast src/app/api/admin/leads/watchlist/route.ts:251). (3) Raw push_token IS selected from the DB (:70, :101) and masked only in JS (:94, :113 via src/lib/admin/mask-push-token.ts:7-15) — the header claim at :8-9 that the full token 'never leaves the server' is true of the HTTP response as written, but nothing structurally enforces it (no view, no column-level guard), so a future added projection could leak it. (4) The three kill-switch/throttle logic variables are surfaced with NO bounds, NO Zod validation and NO type check (:129-134) — a corrupted variable_value is echoed verbatim into meta.gates. (5) `last_dispatch` is taken from dispatches[0] (:118), i.e. the first row of the CURRENT PAGE — with offset>0 and a user_id filter it is the newest dispatch on that page, not the user's newest overall. (6) No SELECT * anywhere. (7) Two sequential awaits (:68 rows, then :86 count) rather than a Promise.all — an avoidable round trip. | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control, no dynamic/revalidate, no in-process memo in route.ts:1-149 | Pagination: limit/offset. Zod-clamped limit [1,200] default 50 and offset >=0 default 0 at src/app/api/admin/notifications/route.ts:25-26; bound as $1/$2 in `LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2` at :82; `total` from a separate COUNT(*) at :86-92, returned in meta at :139. | Other guards / classification: No CSRF check (GET is not a mutating method, src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:45,70). MFA gate inert unless ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED=true (src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:143). | Locking tests: src/tests/admin-notifications.infra.test.ts.
